tally.headline: 1 of 3 gradeable claims held up, 1 did not

implied_side.book: captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers
implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 1.1 points toward Wisconsin of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 46.1 sat 3.4 points below the captured total of 49.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — the spread result changed on the final score — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 2.4 and the game finished 10 the home way — 7.6 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A two-turnover edge
variance_markers.text: Wisconsin Badgers won the turnover battle by two, which is worth roughly a touchdown of scoreboard on average and is largely noise game to game.

variance_markers.label: The spread result changed on the final score
variance_markers.text: Before the last scoring play of the game the spread graded win; it finished loss. A number that moves on a score taken in the last minutes of a decided game is a scoreboard event, not a matchup one.

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning did not either. This is the case that should change something, and the lessons below say what.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: Wisconsin holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: Wisconsin 61.1 (#24 of 138) vs UCLA 51.5 (#134 of 138) — 110 places on the national board.
lessons.actual_result: Wisconsin Badgers 4.13 yards per pass attempt against UCLA Bruins 7.77.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Wisconsin as better in QB and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 27.5 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 9 of the claims in this article rested on model, defence, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the box score for this game published no yards per play.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, defence, passing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 46.1.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 24 points, an error of 22.1.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it UCLA −2.5 where the market has UCLA −3.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers — a 1.1 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: UCLA Bruins won by 10. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: UCLA Bruins beat a margin of -3.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
